title: Robert M. Shive v. Central Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC rejected both claimed errors: the prior decision had not reversed Shive’s four guilty verdicts, and Presbytery properly affirmed Session’s later imposition of excommunication. The appeal was not sustained, leaving the excommunication in effect.
first_summary: A member appealed Presbytery’s affirmance of his excommunication, arguing that an earlier SJC decision had reversed his guilt and barred the increased censure. The SJC did not sustain either issue. It held that the earlier decision reversed only the original excommunication, not the guilty verdicts, and deferred to Session’s determination that he had not provided satisfactory evidence of repentance. The later excommunication therefore remained in effect.
summary: A member challenged Presbytery’s affirmance of his excommunication, contending that SJC Case 97-9 had reversed his four guilty verdicts and precluded increased censure. The SJC did not sustain either issue. Case 97-9 had reversed only the original censure, leaving guilt intact. Because the offender bore the burden of showing repentance, and Session’s contrary factual determination received great deference absent clear error, the later excommunication remained in effect.
